content.text: {"persuasion":"UNPERSUADED","support_scope":"NONE","rationale":"The cited texts consistently present renaming as a God-given change of designation, identity, or status. Genesis 32 marks Jacob’s new standing as Israel; Isaiah 62 explicitly interprets Zion’s renaming through Hephzibah and Beulah, expressing vindication, divine delight, and restored relationship; Isaiah 65 contrasts the condemned community’s name with the designation of God’s servants; and Revelation 2 promises the conqueror a personally received and privately known name. None identifies the new name with a renewed Word or priesthood. A covenant dimension is plausible, but it does not establish the book’s distinctive threefold identification. Revelation 2:17 supports “received” and privately “known,” but not the added claim that the name is uniquely “kept” by its bearer. The transformed-identity/status interpretation therefore accounts for the textual details with fewer unsupported steps.","book_core_identification":"The renewed Name signifies or embodies a renewed Word, covenant, and priesthood.","book_secondary_elaborations":["The Name, Word, covenant, and priesthood are renewed.","The renewed Name is known, received, and kept only by the person who bears it."],"unsupported_glossary_assertions":["That the renewed Name is a renewed Word.","That the renewed Name is a renewed priesthood.","That the Name itself is a renewed covenant, rather than a designation marking covenant restoration or belonging.","That the Name is uniquely “kept” by its bearer; Revelation 2:17 says that the recipient receives and knows it, but does not say that the recipient keeps it."],"chapter_only_objections":[],"strongest_counter_interpretation":"A new name is a divinely bestowed designation marking transformed identity and status—individually for Jacob and Revelation’s conqueror, and corporately for restored Zion—especially covenant belonging, vindication, divine favor, and a changed destiny.","counter_core_identification":"The new name is the designation of a renewed person or people and signifies their changed identity, status, and covenant relationship; it is not itself a renewed Word, covenant, or priesthood.","counter_relation_to_book_core":"CONTRADICTS","material_core_denial":"The counter-reading denies that Word, covenant, and priesthood are the referents of “new name.” It instead identifies the person or covenant community as the renamed referent, with the name expressing that referent’s changed standing.","counter_case":["Genesis 32:28 directly replaces Jacob’s personal designation with Israel and explains the change by his prevailing with God and men; it says nothing about a renewed Word or priesthood.","Isaiah 62:2-5 supplies concrete replacement designations—Hephzibah and Beulah—and explains them as the reversal of being Forsaken and Desolate, public vindication, divine delight, and marital restoration.","Isaiah 65:15 contrasts the cursed former name with another name given to God’s servants, naturally indicating changed communal standing and allegiance.","Revelation 2:17 makes the conqueror the recipient of a privately known name. This supports personal recognition, belonging, or eschatological status without identifying the name as Word, covenant, or priesthood.","The counter-reading accommodates both individual and corporate cases while preserving the common elements across them: divine bestowal, changed designation, changed status, and covenantal vindication."],"book_explanatory_advantages":["It recognizes the covenantal setting shared by Jacob’s renaming, Zion’s restoration, and the conqueror’s reward.","It preserves Revelation 2:17’s emphasis that the name is received and privately known.","Its language of renewal appropriately reflects the contrast between the former and new designations."],"counter_explanatory_advantages":["It follows the immediate referents of the passages: Jacob, Zion or her land, God’s servants, and the individual conqueror.","It explains Isaiah’s actual replacement names and the explicit reversals from Forsaken and Desolate to divine delight and marriage.","It accounts for the public dimension in Isaiah and the private dimension in Revelation without forcing both into an otherwise unattested priesthood referent.","It requires no unprinted symbolic equation between name and Word or between name and priesthood.","It explains why receiving a name changes or declares the bearer’s identity and standing."],"evidence_book_core_cannot_explain":["Isaiah 62 explicitly identifies the renamed subjects as Zion and her land and gives the semantic content of the new designations as Hephzibah and Beulah. Treating the same named referent as a renewed Word or priesthood conflicts with the passage’s own identification.","Genesis 32:28 explicitly presents Jacob as the bearer whose designation becomes Israel; the stated rationale concerns his changed standing after prevailing, not the renewal of a Word or priesthood.","Revelation 2:17 says the recipient receives and knows the name, but supplies no textual basis for the glossary’s additional mechanic of uniquely keeping it."],"comparative_winner":"COUNTER","decisive_sources":["Isaiah 62:2-5","Genesis 32:28","Revelation 2:17","Isaiah 65:15"],"unresolved_objections":["Revelation 2:17 does not disclose the content of the new name, so its exact nuance—personal identity, Christ’s name, ownership, vindication, or an admission credential—remains uncertain.","The covenant element of the book’s entry is partially consonant with the contexts, but the evidence supports covenant status or belonging more directly than identifying the name itself as the covenant."],"confidence":"high"}

support_scope.description: Support for the exact glossary BOOK ENTRY only, never for the supporting chapter as a whole.

book_secondary_elaborations.description: Secondary assertions actually printed in the glossary BOOK ENTRY; exclude chapter-only claims.

unsupported_glossary_assertions.description: Material assertions actually printed in the BOOK ENTRY that the evidence does not support. Must be empty for FULL and nonempty for CORE_ONLY.

chapter_only_objections.description: Objections to applications or arguments found only in the supporting chapter. Preserved for later chapter review and excluded from the glossary scope ruling.
